question.text: An electromagnetic wave is represented by the electric filed <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mo>→</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">E</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow></msub><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">sin</mi></mrow><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mfenced close="]" open="[" separators="|"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ω</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">t</mi><mo>+</mo><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>6</mn><mi>y</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>z</mi></mrow></mfenced></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></mrow></mrow></math> Taking unit vectors in <math><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi></math> and <math><mi>z</mi></math> directions to be <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>i</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>j</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi>k</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi></math> the directions of propogations <math><mover accent="true"><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>,</mo></math> is:

solution.text:
The standard equation of electromagnetic wave E→=E0n^sinωt-kx^

here x^ represents the direction of propagation wave.

On comparing the given equation with the standard equation, the direction of propagation is along line -6y+8z . Thus, unit vector along the direction of propagation is,
s^=-6j^+8k^10=-35j^+45k^
